question.prompt:
Three flower beds overlap as shown. Bed \(A\) has \(500\) plants, bed \(B\) has \(450\) plants, and bed \(C\) has \(350\) plants. Beds \(A\) and \(B\) share \(50\) plants, while beds \(A\) and \(C\) share \(100.\) The total number of plants is

[Figure 1](figures/1999_AMC_8_Q09_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The diagram shows that beds \(B\) and \(C\) do not overlap. We can therefore count bed \(A\) first, then add only the new plants from each other bed.

Count all \(500\) plants in \(A\). Of the \(450\) plants in \(B\), the \(50\) shared with \(A\) have already been counted, leaving \(450-50=400\) new plants. Similarly, \(C\) contributes \(350-100=250\) new plants. None of these new plants from \(C\) belongs to \(B\), because those two beds do not overlap.

These groups include every plant exactly once, so the total is
\[
500+400+250=1150.
\]
There are \(\boxed{1150}\) plants, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Add only plants not already counted
